newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish NKT in North Sea cable project.
newsitem.headline: Danish NKT in North Sea cable project.

text.p: Danish wire and cable manufacturer NKT Holding A/S said on Wednesday it signed a contract to develop and provide high tension cables for a 1.5-2.0 billion crown North Sea undersea cable project linking the Netherlands with Norway.
It said its partners in the NorNed project were Norway's Statnett S.F. and the Netherlands' N.V. Samenwerkende Elektriciteits-Produktiebedrijven (Sep).
NKT said that after an initial one-year development period it would deliver the cables to NorNed from next year until the scheduled completion of the project in 2001.
NorNed involves laying 570 km of cable under the North Sea off the coasts of the Netherlands, Germany and Denmark and below the Skagerrak to Norway at depths of 400 metres in places, it said.
NKT managing director Gerhard Albrechtsen told Reuters that the group was optimistic about making major earnings from European cable projects in coming years.

"There are many North Sea cable projects afoot, among them links between Germany and Norway and Scotland and Norway and we reckon that intercontinental high tension cables will be in great demand," he said.
